title: Tamil Nadu's New CM Vijay Shuts 717 TASMAC Shops
excerpt: Actor-turned-Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay orders closure of liquor outlets near temples, schools, and bus stands within two weeks of taking office.
body:
Just one day after taking oath as Tamil Nadu's Chief Minister, C. Joseph Vijay signed one of his first major orders: the closure of 717 state-run TASMAC liquor shops across the state, all located within 500 metres of places of worship, educational institutions, or bus stands.

**What Vijay ordered:**
The directive, issued on May 11, 2026, targets three categories of proximity violations. Of the 717 outlets marked for shutdown, 276 sit near temples and places of worship, 186 are close to schools and colleges, and 255 adjoin bus stands. TASMAC currently operates approximately 4,765 retail liquor outlets statewide, and all flagged shops must close within two weeks of the order.

**Why this matters:**
TAMSAC — the Tamil Nadu State Marketing Corporation — holds a complete monopoly over the wholesale and retail sale of alcohol in the state, making it a formidable political and financial institution. Vijay's Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) party broke nearly six decades of alternating DMK-AIADMK rule after the April 23 assembly elections, and the new CM is moving fast to signal a governance shift. The previous DMK government under M.K. Stalin had itself closed 500 TASMAC outlets in June 2023, and the Madras High Court had separately criticised the government for opening new shops near sensitive locations. Vijay's order goes further, using a location-based criterion that applies uniformly across all five TASMAC regions.

**What to watch:**
Whether Vijay's coalition — which controls only a slim majority of 120 seats in the 234-member assembly — can sustain pressure for broader prohibition reform, and how TASMAC's substantial contribution to the state exchequer shapes the pace of future closures.
